absent: Locking and concurrency rules for ramfs inode allocation, dentry installation, and parent timestamp updates.
Full address space operation set and reclaim behavior for ramfs mappings, including unevictable interaction with memory pressure.
Detailed validation performed by the nommu shared mapping shrink helper when truncating over mapped ranges.
Security policy outcomes for inode initialization beyond propagation of its error code.
Exact numeric values and architecture dependence of page order limits, page size, maximum read write count, and seek bounds.
Implementation of generic helpers for folio gathering, vector import, range verification, and notification owned by other dossiers.
Ordering and idempotency guarantees for filesystem context teardown and anonymous superblock destruction.
Behavior of read paths corresponding to the write dispatch shown, including caching and access notification details.

findings.text: Provides an operation that prepares a ramfs inode store for nommu shared mapping at a requested byte length. A zero length request succeeds without further work. Excessively large requests that would need an allocation order beyond the system maximum are rejected, as are sizes that fail inode size validation. On success the inode size reflects the request and its address space holds enough zero filled resident pages to cover the size, each marked dirty and up to date and left unlocked with cache references balanced. Allocation failure and page cache insertion failure are reported to the caller, with unused or not yet attached pages released.

Defines how ramfs on nommu systems reacts to a size change from a current size to a new size. A growth starting from zero is treated as preparation for shared mapping and is delegated to the mapping expansion path with rejection of values that do not fit in thirty two bits. A shrink that could amputate existing shared mappings first asks the nommu mapping shrink helper to validate and fails if that helper fails. Otherwise the new size is installed through the generic truncate size setter.

Describes attribute update handling for nommu ramfs inodes. Permission and preparation checks run first. When a size attribute is present and differs from the current size, the resize path is invoked, while a size only update or a resize failure ends processing without further attribute copying. When the size is unchanged the update is converted into timestamp refresh. Other attributes are installed through the generic attribute copy helper, and the caller visible validity mask is restored before return.

Specifies how a nommu ramfs file backs a request for an unmapped area. The requested byte length is rounded up to whole pages and compared against the file size expressed in pages, with requests starting at or beyond end of file or extending past it rejected. Folios backing the requested file offset range are collected in batches and examined for physical contiguity across folio boundaries. The address of the first folio becomes the candidate result only if every subsequent folio continues the expected physical sequence and enough pages accumulate, while any gap, missing folio set, or shortfall yields an unsupported error and releases batch references.

Gates nommu ramfs mapping preparation on shared mapping semantics. Private or otherwise non shared flag combinations are rejected. Accepted mappings record file access and are associated with the generic file virtual memory operations before reporting success.

Mount configuration for ramfs consists of a small options record holding a mode value and a filesystem info record holding that options record. The inode and super operation tables are forward declared for later definition in the same translation unit.
Default mount mode is octal 0755.

Creates and initializes a fresh ramfs inode for a superblock with optional parent directory context, mode, and device number. Fresh inodes receive a new inode number, ownership derived from parent and mode, address space operations for ram storage with high user allocation mask and unevictable marking, and current timestamps. Type dispatch wires regular files to ramfs file operations, directories to ramfs directory operations with an extra link for dot, symlinks to page symlink operations with low memory restriction, and other types to special inode setup.

Unifies ramfs directory entry creation around a common node maker. The maker allocates an inode, runs security initialization with the parent and name, makes the dentry persistent on success, and refreshes parent timestamps, reporting no space when allocation fails and propagating security errors with inode release. Directory creation adds a parent link, regular creation forces regular type, symlink creation sizes the target plus terminator and stores it through the page symlink helper, and temporary file creation attaches an anonymous inode to an open file and completes it through the simple open finish helper which either propagates its error input or finishes opening against the file dentry.
Ramfs directory inode behavior combines ramfs specific handlers for file directory symlink node and temporary creation with shared simple helpers for lookup link unlink directory removal and rename.

Superblock behavior for ramfs delegates statistics, inode dropping, and option display to simple or trivial helpers, showing a mode option only when it differs from default. Mount parameters accept an octal mode value masked to permission bits, unknown source style parameters are delegated to the generic source parser, and any other unknown option is silently ignored for compatibility with historical behavior and use as a simple tmpfs substitute.

Superblock instantiation sets a large maximum file size, page sized blocks, ramfs magic, ramfs super operations, no cache dentry behavior, and one unit time granularity, then creates a root directory inode with the configured mode and makes it the root dentry, failing when the root cannot be built. Tree acquisition uses a no device helper, context management frees filesystem info, and context operations wire free parse and tree handlers.

Filesystem lifecycle exposes context initialization that allocates info with default mode and wires context operations, superblock teardown that frees info and kills an anonymous super, a filesystem type record advertising ramfs identity with user namespace mount support and its parameter table, and an init routine that registers that type.
Read only generic file behavior offers lease management, seek, splice read, vectored read, and read only mapping preparation through generic helpers.

Fixed size, end unaware, and no operation seek helpers provide constrained positioning. Fixed size seeks accept only set current and end relative to a supplied size. End unaware variants accept only set and current against either an unbounded maximum or a supplied size. The no operation variant leaves position unchanged and reports the current offset. Unsupported whence values are rejected.

Generic seek implements a whence machine over set current end data and hole. End is resolved against current file size, current leaves a zero offset as a query and otherwise adds position, data succeeds for offsets before size and fails at or beyond it, and hole reports size for offsets before it and fails at or beyond it. Negative results are rejected unless unsigned offsets are permitted, otherwise a changed position is stored and reported.
Generic seek serializes size and position handling under a killable inode lock held from entry until after position update, with early query and error paths releasing through a common unlock.

Seek entry points validate descriptors and whence bounds before delegating to the virtual seek helper. The native path reports overflow when the result does not fit the native offset type, the compatibility path shares the same logic with a narrower offset, and the split high low path combines halves into a full offset and copies the result back to user memory, distinguishing copy failure from seek failure.

Write dispatch enforces write mode and writability capability, validates user buffer accessibility, verifies the range, clamps excessive counts to the maximum read write count, and then prefers a legacy write handler when present, falling back to a synchronous iterator wrapper that drives write iteration and advances the supplied position on success while asserting asynchronous queuing never occurs. Successful writes trigger modify notification and accounting under paired write section markers.
Write side paths bracket handler invocation with filesystem write freeze protection, acquiring before dispatch and releasing afterwards, including error and unsupported operation paths.

Stream files use no persistent position while other files use the open file offset. Kernel read and write helpers snapshot that offset when present, delegate to the byte paths, and commit the advanced offset only on success, reporting bad descriptor when lookup fails. The read and write system entries are thin delegations to those helpers.

Positional read and write entries reject negative offsets and missing descriptors, require pread or pwrite capability respectively, and otherwise delegate to the byte paths with an explicit offset, reporting pipe style error when positional operation is unsupported.

Vectored byte paths enforce read or write mode and capability, import user vectors with a small on stack fast path, ignore empty total length after import, and verify the range. When an iterator handler exists it is used, otherwise a loop helper drives legacy single segment handlers, rejecting flags beyond high priority, accumulating progress, stopping on error or short transfer, and advancing the iterator.

Descriptor level vectored wrappers snapshot file position for non stream files, delegate to the byte vectored paths, commit position on success, and apply read or write accounting with system call counters. Positional variants validate non negative offsets, require positional capability, and otherwise share the same delegation and accounting. The readv and writev system entries are thin wrappers that invoke the non positional path with no extra flags.
Split position composition treats a machine word as two equal halves and shifts the high half by half the word width before combining with the low half.

Several boundary behaviors merit care. Inode size is updated before page allocation completes so failure can leave size ahead of backing store. Excess high order pages are freed after splitting. Cache insertion failure frees only not yet attached pages while already attached pages stay in cache. Mapping area lookup can retry across batches and fails when physical contiguity breaks. Seek overflow is possible on narrow types. Data and hole queries fail at or beyond size. Vectored loops may return partial success.
